name: Constellation Energy
thesis: World's largest private power producer (55 GW post-Calpine) with the nation's premier nuclear fleet (22 GW, 183 TWh zero-emissions generation in 2025). FY2025 revenue $25.5B (+8% YoY) with adjusted EPS of $9.39. Calpine acquisition closed Jan 7, 2026 for $16.4B, adding 23 GW of natural gas and geothermal generation, promising 20%+ EPS accretion. Guided 2026 adjusted EPS to $11.00-12.00 with 20% CAGR commitment through 2029. Key datacenter PPAs: Microsoft (Crane Clean Energy Center restart, 20-year PPA), Meta (Clinton nuclear, 1.1 GW), CyrusOne (380 MW). Stock down ~13% YTD as guidance disappointed vs Street expectations, creating potential entry point. $5B share buyback authorized.
catalysts: Calpine integration delivering 20%+ EPS accretion — Q1 2026 EBITDA consensus $2.02B (+139% sequential)
2026 adjusted EPS guidance $11-12 with 20% CAGR commitment through 2029
Crane Clean Energy Center restart (835 MW) backed by 20-year Microsoft PPA
Nuclear license renewals: Clinton extended to 2047, Dresden to 2049/2051 — $370M invested
$5B share buyback program authorized — significant capital return
risks: Crane Clean Energy Center interconnection flagged for potential delay to 2031 by PJM — threatens Microsoft PPA
Calpine integration complexity: 2,300 employees, 60+ power plants, rising interest expense from $16.4B financing
2026 guidance midpoint ($11.50 EPS) below initial Street consensus ($11.73) — sent stock down 7%
Nuclear operational risk across 22 GW fleet — unplanned outages impact earnings
Regulatory and policy risk: clean energy subsidies, capacity market reforms, PJM interconnection rules

name: Vertiv
thesis: Dominant datacenter thermal management and power distribution leader riding the AI infrastructure supercycle. Q1 2026 revenue $2.65B (+30% YoY) with adjusted EPS of $1.17 (+83% YoY). FY2025 revenue reached $10.2B (+28% YoY) with $1.3B net income (+169%). Backlog surged to $15.0B (+109% YoY) with Q4 2025 book-to-bill of 2.9x driven by 252% organic orders growth. Adjusted operating margin expanded to 20.8% in Q1 2026 (+430bps YoY). Raised 2026 guidance to $13.5-14.0B revenue (+34% growth) with adj. EPS of $6.30-6.40 (+51%). Net leverage at 0.2x with $5.0B liquidity. CoolPhase Flex hybrid cooling and 800VDC power solutions position Vertiv at the center of the liquid cooling transition for 100+ kW AI racks.
catalysts: $15.0B backlog (+109% YoY) with book-to-bill of 2.9x — orders accelerating, not decelerating
2026 guidance raised to $13.5-14.0B revenue (+34% growth), adj. EPS $6.30-6.40 (+51%)
Q1 2026 adjusted free cash flow $653M (+147% YoY) — cash generation inflecting sharply
Liquid cooling supercycle: CoolPhase Flex and 800VDC solutions for NVIDIA next-gen GPU racks
Adjusted operating margin expansion to 22.8-23.8% guided for FY2026 (+290bps vs FY2025)
risks: Premium valuation at ~42x forward P/E and $131B market cap — priced for perfection
Hyperscaler customer concentration — top customers drive outsized revenue share
Execution risk on 34% revenue growth with simultaneous margin expansion
STL acquisition integration risk alongside organic growth demands
Potential demand moderation if hyperscaler capex cycle decelerates

name: Bloom Energy
thesis: Market-leading solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) manufacturer with dominant datacenter power positioning. Q1 2026 revenue $751M (+130% YoY) — record quarter. Oracle expanded master agreement to 2.8 GW. FY2025 revenue $2.02B (+37%). First GAAP net income achieved in Q1 2026 ($70.7M). 2026 guidance raised to $3.4-3.8B (~80% growth). Fuel flexibility (natural gas, hydrogen, biogas) and rapid deployment (55-day installation for Oracle) are key differentiators for grid-constrained datacenter sites.
catalysts: Oracle 2.8 GW master agreement — initial 1.2 GW contracted, deployment underway
Q1 2026 revenue $751M (+130% YoY) — first GAAP profit ($70.7M net income)
2026 guidance raised to $3.4-3.8B revenue (~80% growth at midpoint)
55-day deployment speed for Oracle — month ahead of schedule
risks: Stock up ~240% YTD — valuation stretched at $82B market cap
Oracle customer concentration risk in near-term
Long-term debt of $2.6B vs $2.5B cash — elevated leverage
Competition from grid power, gas turbines for baseload datacenter
Hydrogen transition timeline uncertain for SOFC platform

name: Plug Power
thesis: Hydrogen fuel cell and electrolyzer company pivoting to datacenter backup power. FY2025 revenue $710M (+13% YoY), first positive gross margin in Q4 2025. Targeting datacenter fuel cell deployments with all three hyperscalers. Cash-burn remains significant ($536M operating outflow in 2025) with only $368M unrestricted cash. Management targets positive EBITDAS by Q4 2026 and full profitability by end of 2028.
catalysts: Datacenter pivot: LOI with Stream Data Centers for $132.5M+ asset monetization supporting DC buildout
First positive gross margin achieved Q4 2025 — inflection point
Electrolyzer sales reached $187M in FY2025, growing sequentially
$275M+ monetization of electricity rights to support datacenter build-out
Testing with all three major hyperscalers for fuel cell backup power
risks: Severe cash burn: $536M operating cash outflow in 2025 with only $368M cash remaining
Profitability not expected until end of 2028 — multi-year path
Stock trading near all-time lows (~$3.08) — dilution risk from capital raises
Hydrogen cost economics still unproven at datacenter scale
Competition from Bloom Energy (SOFC) and diesel generators

name: FuelCell Energy
thesis: Carbonate fuel cell manufacturer pivoting aggressively to datacenter power. Q1 FY2026 revenue $30.5M (+61% YoY). 1.5 GW datacenter pipeline with 275% growth since Feb 2025. New 12.5 MW standardized power blocks for rapid datacenter deployment. SDCL partnership for 450 MW identified projects. Tri-gen technology produces electricity, hydrogen, and heat (absorption cooling for DC thermal management). Still pre-profit with $192M operating loss in FY2025, but $379.6M cash provides runway.
catalysts: Datacenter pipeline 1.5+ GW with 275% growth — SDCL partnership for 450 MW
New 12.5 MW standardized power block for rapid datacenter deployment (months, not years)
Q1 FY2026 revenue +61% YoY to $30.5M — accelerating growth
Tri-gen technology: electricity + hydrogen + absorption cooling for DC thermal loads
Manufacturing expansion planned: 100 MW to 350 MW capacity at Torrington, CT
risks: $1.17B backlog declining 10.8% — revenue recognized faster than new awards
Still deeply unprofitable: $192M operating loss in FY2025, net loss $7.42/share
Dilution risk: $56.3M raised via at-the-market stock sales in Q1 2026
Small revenue base ($158M FY2025) relative to datacenter power ambitions
Competition from Bloom Energy, natural gas generators, and grid power
